text:
dana: Heads-up — caught a TP all-reduce regression on staging after the KV cache packing tweak. latency for tp all-reduce jumps ~2.6x on small msgs.
liam: ugh. is this the small-msg path where we fallback to tree?
sophia: probably. saw something similar when packing threshold lowered. do we have profiles?
dana: yes, attached quick profiling snapshot from nsys (stripped):
```
# nsys summary
ALLREDUCE (nccl): calls=112, avg=0.92ms -> 2.35ms after change
ring_allreduce kernels: 0.62ms
tree_allreduce kernels: 1.85ms
comm/compute overlap dropped from 45% -> 12%
msg size histogram: 10KB: 78%, 128KB: 12%, 512KB: 10%
```
jamal: so msgsize distribution shifted towards small bins after kv-packing because we're breaking prefixes into smaller fragments?
yuan: yea the new kv-coalesce window tries to flush earlier to avoid head-of-line, but it produces more fragments per sequence, and NCCL chooses tree for <~32KB in our kernel selector.
liam: interesting — tree is higher latency for tiny msgs? i thought tree helped small ones.
sophia: tree reduces bandwidth for very small point-to-point, but our implementation's extra synchronization and rendezvous for TP allreduce kills overlap. ring keeps steady streaming which overlaps with compute better.
dana: confirm. local trace shows a 3x increase in idle CPU waiting on allreduce start handshake when tree is chosen.
jamal: can we force ring for the problematic range and see perf? quick A/B.
yuan: patch to kernel selector ready: change threshold from 32KB -> 8KB for tree fallback. rolling it on canary now. test command is:
```
# repro command (tp8)
python -m tools/run_tp_bench --model=gpt-medium --tp 8 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --profile --msgpack-config=kv_coalesce_window=10ms
```
liam: run that with --nccl-profiling too, capture op shapes.
sophia: also try padding small messages to 64KB to see cost of coalescing vs padding. my hunch: padding gives better end-to-end latency than tree fallback.
dana: I spun up canary with selector change. short results: overall latency down ~18%, but tail p50->p95 still sketchy in presence of uneven token splits.
jamal: can we improve batching heuristic instead? combine adjacent small fragments into single allreduce call before issuing?
yuan: possible. would need move-level aggregator in runtime; tricky for KV cache because coherence depends on order. however a cheap heuristic: delay flush by 2ms to let coalescing happen, only when backlog < X.
liam: risk: adds latency for single-token low-latency requests. need a smart adaptive window.
sophia: action items:
- dana/yuan: keep ring-first threshold patch on canary, collect nccl profiles over 24h (ACTION-1)
- jamal: prototype 2ms coalesce delay in runtime and measure worst-case added latency (ACTION-2)
- liam: add a perf test that simulates skewed token splits and KV-fragment-heavy workloads (ACTION-3)
- everyone: post traces to /shared/tp-allreduce/regressions/3501234567 (attach links here)
dana: i'll paste initial trace link when ready. perf-bot: scheduled nightly collection for canary cluster (job id: nb-7921). :robot_face:
perf-bot: job nb-7921 started: collecting nccl and nsys traces (24h)
yuan: one more note — kernel autoswitch also picks different CUDA kernels when sequence length << typical; combined with tree/ring change we saw kernel mismatch thrashing. check kernel-selector logs: set --kernel-verbose true.
dana: good call. thanks all, will update once we have 24h data. :thumbsup:
